2. The petitioner has been made accused in connection Simdega P.S. Case No. 60 of 2009, G.R. Case No. 173 of 2009, S.T. No. 80 of 2023 registered for offences punishable under Sections 376 of the I.P.C. which is pending in the Court of Learned Additional Sessions Judge- 1st, Simdega.

entities.text: Court of Learned Additional Sessions Judge- 1st, Simdega
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. As per F.I.R., on 08.06.2009 at about 5.00. P.M. the cousin brother (Mausera Bhai) victim (blind)
came to her house with three unknown persons and after taking meal and consuming alcohol, her cousin brother had gone with his two friends on motorcycle towards Farsa Bera.
The mother of the victim and her two brothers had gone to attend the funeral of one woman in the village.

At that time,
the victim and one friend of her cousin brother were alone at the house and committed rape upon the victim (blind).
On hearing the screams of her sister, the villagers assembled there and caught that person.

Thereafter, one meeting was convened in the village in presence of parents of the accused, in which a fine of Rs.8,000/- was imposed upon the accused, out of which Rs.2,000/- was deposited by the accused to the Punch Members.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and he has falsely been implicated in this case.
Petitioner is in judicial custody since 17.06.2023.
Petitioner has no criminal antecedent and charge-sheet has been submitted against the petitioner.

Petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the trial of the case and to remain physically present on each and every date till the conclusion of the trial and shall not indulge in tampering with the prosecution evidence or influence the witnesses or gain over them.
Hence, the petitioner may be enlarged on bail.
5. Learned Addl. P.P. has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner and submitted that the petitioner has committed rape upon a blind girl.
Hence, petitioner does not deserve to be Xavier Barla @ Xavier Tete vs The State Of Jharkhand ...

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, I am not inclined to admit the petitioner on bail, which stands rejected.
7. The learned Trial Court is directed to expedite the trial of the case and conclude within three months otherwise petitioner shall be at liberty to renew his prayer for bail.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Amar/-
